guards.what: the Sea Glass character pick (Orobas.cs:59-62): `base.Rng.NextItem(UnlockState.Characters.Where(c => c.Id != character.Id))`, falling back to the player's own character on null
guards.maps_to: events/orobas.py:54-55 draws next_item over ALL_CHARACTERS minus Ironclad and DISCARDS the result. That is right for two reasons the record should state together: the draw itself must happen (dropping it would shift all three later picks off the same stream), and its value only selects which character's Sea Glass is offered -- a relic whose payload is another character's pool and therefore a documented stub in an Ironclad-only sim. The fully-unlocked convention makes the candidate set the full ModelDb.AllCharacters minus Ironclad, matching the pools' convention (events/orobas.py:25-28).

guards.what: the Prismatic Gem / Sea Glass roll (Orobas.cs:65-71): `base.Rng.NextFloat() < 0.3333333f` picks the Gem, else a Sea Glass for the character rolled above; the winner is APPENDED to OptionPool1 before the first pick
guards.maps_to: events/orobas.py:56-59 in the same order -- the float draw comes after the character draw and before the three NextItem picks -- and appends to pool1 rather than replacing. NOTE the constant: C# is the float literal `0.3333333f`, the sim is `1 / 3` = 0.3333333333333333. A draw landing in the ~3.3e-8 window between them would diverge; recorded rather than waived because it is a real if vanishingly narrow difference, and it costs nothing to pin the literal if a seed ever lands there.

guards.what: OptionPool3's LOCKED path skips an RNG draw. Orobas.cs:54-56 adds a null-onChosen OPTION_POOL_3_LOCKED option INTO the list when both gates fail, and Orobas.cs:75 then calls `base.Rng.NextItem(OptionPool3)` unconditionally -- so the game takes a NextItem draw over a one-element list
guards.issue: events/orobas.py:76-81 branches instead: `if pool3: pick(pool3) else: EventOption('OPTION_POOL_3_LOCKED', None)`. The locked branch never calls pick, so the sim takes ONE FEWER draw off the event stream than the game does. The offered options are identical -- the locked option is the only candidate either way -- so this is invisible in legacy mode, but in a string-seeded parity run it desyncs the event stream for the rest of that event and any later consumer of it. LIVE for the parity path: the both-gates-fail state is ordinary (a run with no Touch-of-Orobas-refinable starter and no transcendence card in the deck), and Orobas is one of the three act-2 Ancients.
